summary.text: A female patient aged 13 years with neural tube defects, VP-shunt, neurogenic bladder, chronic renal insufficiency and hypertension on intermittent catheterization and prophylactic antibiotics presented with fever, vomiting and malodorous urine; a first Morganella morganii urinary tract infection was managed as an outpatient. Imaging showed an atrophic left kidney, a hydronephrotic right kidney, a trabeculated bladder and grade III right vesicoureteral reflux. A second M. morganii infection occurred at age 16 years; she was an inpatient, treated with meropenem and teicoplanin before culture and meropenem after culture, continued for 20 days because of persistent pyuria.

article_limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.
